Coal royalty payments will have major impacts on Crow income.

According to lease agreements, Westmoreland Resources will make royalty payments to the Crow Tribe based on a percentage of the FOB mine sales price. The amount of these payments are given in Table III-5 for each of the production levels. Under Westmoreland's most probable production plan (Scenario 1) royalty payments will be $1.5 million in 1976, reach $7.5 million in 1982, and build up to nearly $11.8 million by 1994. For the higher production level (Scenario 2), royalty payments reach the highest level for any scenario, $16 million in 1994. The projected royalty payments take on special significance when it is considered that total Crow Tribal income in 1975 was $2,636,152 (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 f p. 390).
It is not known what the Crow Tribe will do with the royalty income, which nearly doubles by 1977 and increases several-fold by 2000. There are two general alternatives: the entire amount may be given in per capita payments to members of the Tribe; or the Tribe may disburse a portion of the royalties in per capita payments and use the rest for investments and improvements for the Tribe as a whole. The second alternative, which has many possible combinations, is oriented toward long-range economic return. Tribal leaders appear to understand the merit of such an approach.
